headline: Discussed a statewide emergency ban on Kratom sales and a federal lawsuit over tobacco retailer rules; approved July minutes.
summary: Health Agent David Greenbaum updated members on a state emergency order that bans Kratom sales for up to one year. He said Peabody and Beverly have adopted Kratom bans, and members heard about a federal lawsuit over tobacco sales rules and a draft Bodyworks regulation. Members approved the July 14, 2026 minutes by a 4-0 vote.
decisions: Approved the July 14, 2026 minutes by a 4-0 vote.

decision_evidence.quote: D. Elias motioned to approve the minutes S. Lunde 2nd. All in favor. Motion passed by a vote of 4 to 0.

1 | P a g e 
 
 
 
                                                                    CITY OF SALEM  
BOARD OF HEALTH 
MEETING MINUTES 
 
September 8, 2026 
 
MEMBERS PRESENT: Sara Moore, Chair, Datanis Elias, Sean Lunde, Marie Feldmannova 
                                          
MEMBERS EXCUSED: Jeremy Schiller 
 
OTHERS PRESENT: David Greenbaum, Health Agent,  
   
TOPIC DISCUSSION/ACTION 
  
1. Call to Order 
 
2. Approval of Minutes 
         (July 14, 2026) 
 
 
 
3. Discussion and update 
regarding the emergency order 
from the MA Department of 
Public Health banning the sale 
of Kratom in the 
Commonwealth of MA. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
4. Update regarding the 
manufacture’s granted order 
policy and the federal lawsuit 
filed by the tobacco retailers. 
7:00pm 
 
D. Elias motioned to approve the minutes S. Lunde 2nd. All in favor. 
 
Motion passed by a vote of 4 to 0.  
 
 
D. Greenbaum updated the Boad regarding the emergency order issued by 
the Commissioner of Public Health regarding Kratom.  This order bans the 
sale of Kratom in all forms for up to one year in the Commonwealth.  He 
has not heard that this will be extended, but he did anticipate during that 
one-year timeframe, there probably would be something more permanent. 
He advised the Board that Peabody and Beverly have also adopted 
regulations banning the sale of Kratom.  Marblehead, Swampscott, and 
Lynn are also looking at regulations.  That would make six of the eight 
north shore communities that are looking at regulations. 
S. Moore asked if there were any other states that had completely banned 
Kratom. 
D. Greenbaum explained that New Hampshire was looking at a ban 
synthetic Kratom, but he did not know the status of that ban.  He also did 
know of any other states that had banned Kratom. 
S. Moore asked if we have heard of any stores still having Kratom.   
D. Greenbaum explained that he had not heard of any stores still carrying 
Kratom.   He added that the inspectors will be checking for this while out 
on inspection and Joyce is also checking while doing her inspections. 
S. Moore stated she was glad the Board made the decision ahead the 
announcement from the Department of Public Health.  D. Greenbaum 
added that this is a temporary order from the Commissioner, and the Board 
made a permanent decision. 
S. Lunde stated that we do not know where the statewide data is going to 
go, and the state did not include all the other novel intoxicating products. 
 
D. Greenbaum updated the Board on the status of the federal lawsuit from 
tobacco retailers regarding the FDA manufacturer’s marketing grated 
orders.  The Board passed this policy back in June and it became effective 
on July 1.
2 | P a g e 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
5. Public Health Announcements 
/Reports/Updates 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
6. Chairperson Communications 
 
7. Administrative Report 
 
8. Council Liaison Updates 
 
9. New Business/Scheduling of 
Future Agenda Items 
 
On July 1, 16 communities, along with the MA Department of Public 
Health and the Commissioner himself were named in a federal lawsuit 
saying that we did not have the authority to enforce federal regulations, 
which we are not doing.  What the communities are saying is that retailers 
must comply with federal regulations as a requirement of their tobacco 
sales permit.  He stated that the communities worked with the Attorney 
General's office to file the response. He believed that had been done.  He 
explained that the communities agreed that they will not enforce this policy 
or look for any violations until the lawsuit has been resolved. 
S. Moore asked if we have a sense of the timeline for this case.  D. 
Greenbaum explained that he did not.  He thought that the Attorney 
General was looking for response, but he did not know how long that 
would take. He did not know if there would be oral arguments, or if this 
was all going to be filed by paper. 
S. Moore asked if there is any update regarding Bunghole Liquors.   
D. Greenbaum saw that the property owner was suing the owner of the 
liquor store, but he did not know what the status of that was.  
S. Moore asked if there was still an outstanding payment.  D. Greenbaum 
that they had paid that fine.  He explained to the Board what had happened 
and how we were able to hold the permit unit all outstanding fines had been 
paid.   
S. Moore asked if there were any updates regarding the Maitland Mountain 
Farm.  D. Greenbaum explained that he and Mr. Varela were supposed to 
connect in June, but something came up and we could not connect. He does 
need to finalize that matter. They have been making a lot of progress, and 
he has not heard anything further from the neighbor. 
 
D. Greenbaum advised the Board that the City Solicitor’s office has been 
working on Bodyworks Regulations.  He explained that massage therapy is 
permitted by the state.  There was an issue back in January where some 
illicit activity was going on in an unlicensed massage therapy, body works 
type establishment. The City Solicitor looked to see what other 
communities have for regulations for these types of establishments.  This 
would include things like reflexology and Reiki.  The Solicitor's office put 
together a draft regulation that they sent to him. He has reviewed it and sent 
his comments back to them.  This regulation may be coming to the Board 
in the next few months. 
He advised the Board that there may be a corresponding Board of Health 
regulation that was supposed to have been written in conjunction with the 
City Council’s camping ordinance. He stated the City Solicitor was 
working on that, and he would check the status of the regulation when he 
returned
